analysis.description: This paper introduces a novel self-supervised attention module designed to improve reinforcement learning (RL). The proposed method learns attention masks to identify salient regions without explicit annotations, facilitating better policy learning by integrating with existing RL methods. Through a self-supervised loss, the module enables improved convergence speed and performance across both single-task and multi-task settings, showing significant generalization and transfer capabilities. Additionally, the paper demonstrates the ability to extract meaningful object keypoints from the learned masks.

type.justification: The paper involves empirical evaluation of the proposed self-supervised attention module on various RL tasks and compares performance metrics with baselines.
type.quote: We empirically show that the self-supervised attention-aware deep RL methods outperform the baselines in the context of both the rate of convergence and performance.
